notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Filings: FY2025 Form 10-K (accession 0000037996-26-000015, filed February 11, 2026) and the 2026 proxy statement (accession 0001552781-26-000164, filed March 27, 2026), both read on www.sec.gov. Ford's 10-K columns run 2023, 2024, 2025 (left to right). HENRY FORD: deceased founder, so pctEconomic is null. FAMILY: the 2026 proxy lists a voting trust with 70,778,212 Class B shares (99.90% of Class B) as of February 1, 2026. Its trustees are Edsel B. Ford II, William Clay Ford, Jr., Benson Ford, Jr. and Alfred B. Ford. The proxy names William Clay Ford, Jr. (Executive Chair) as a Ford family member and refers to 'the Ford family's more than 121 years of active involvement with and stewardship of the Company'. Holders of Class B Stock together have 40% of the general voting power. The proxy gives no percentage of all shares for the trust, so family.pctEconomic is null rather than derived. For reference, the trust's 70,778,212 Class B shares compare with 3,940,230,185 common plus 70,852,076 Class B shares outstanding at March 16, 2026. Individual Class B holders listed in the proxy (Edsel B. Ford II 6.56%, Lynn F. Alandt 8.84%, David P. Larsen as trustee 14.52%) are not added, because they overlap the voting trust's total. Ford family directors' own common-stock holdings are not added either. HOLDERS: percentages are of common stock only (Class B is under 2% of all shares). The proxy says that as of December 31, 2025 these entities had more than 5%, but the share counts come from Schedules 13G/A filed on different dates (Vanguard April 30, 2025; State Street January 29, 2024, stale; BlackRock July 17, 2025), so asOf is null. State Street's 8.41% includes the 3.5% it holds as trustee of the Ford defined contribution plans master trust, which is held for employees. DIVIDENDS are payments on Common and Class B Stock, including dividend equivalents. BUYBACKS: none in 2025 (the cash-flow line shows a dash). PLAN: null; no broad employee stock purchase plan is described in the 10-K. STOCK COMP: the cash-flow add-back of $510m is pre-tax.

footprint.notes: Ford publishes no state-by-state jobs or investment table that was found. Its corporate.ford.com Global Offices & Plants page lists each plant with approximate employees (U.S., Canadian and Mexican plants marked "Headcount data from June 2026"; others undated; rechecked 2026-11-24 with the same figures); per-state totals are not derived from it, so selected plants appear as sites. The FY2025 10-K gives ~169,000 employees worldwide with no regional split, says Ford and consolidated entities use over 409 operations facilities across 27 countries and 42 manufacturing and assembly plants, and names joint-venture plants (e.g. Türkiye, Thailand, China) without counts. Ford's corporate economic-impact page (corporate.ford.com/social-impact/economic-impact.html) returned only site navigation in its static HTML in the earlier research (not rechecked in this refresh), so its body could not be read; no state-level U.S. investment figures were found on the Ford pages that could be read. Long-lived assets by country (Dec 31, 2025): U.S., Canada, UK, Mexico and All Other. The Saarlouis Body and Assembly Plant site was removed: the FY2025 10-K says Ford ceased Focus production there in the fourth quarter of 2025 and plans to repurpose the facility into a technical center (the plants page still lists it).
